source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 29 aprilie — «Sfântul Nectarie de la Optina»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Νεκτάριος της Όπτινα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», and it is plainly the same man: the elder of Optina, Nicholas Tikhonov in the world. **The two calendars keep him thirteen days apart and the row records the day of the page it quotes.** The corpus's Romanian row keeps him on 29 April from doxologia.ro, and saint.gr keeps him on 12 May; 29 April plus thirteen is 12 May, so the difference is the old and new style of one Russian day and not two commemorations — but both rows are `revised-julian` on their own sources' word, so **nothing is moved and neither row is altered**, and the reading is set down here for the writer. **He is none of the corpus's other men of the name** — Nectarios of Aegina, of Bitola, of Vryoula, the protopsaltes of Prodromou, the Nectarius of 17 May — whom the namesweep flagged and which were read; this is the folder the Romanian pass made for the Optina elder himself. **The Greek adds the years the corpus does not hold**, «(1853 - 1928)» in its head line, with a birth at Yelets in the province of Oryol; the existing folder carries no `dates` object and it is not given one here, the years standing in this note and in the added paragraph instead. **No hymn**: what the page prints below the life is a long block of his sayings and a letter of his own, signed «Ιερομόναχος Νεκτάριος», not a service.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (20 September 2026).
